channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Disentangling the effect of space and electric field on photoelectrochemical water splitting
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77786-5

Photoelectrochemical performance strongly depends on charge separation within space charge layer, but the precise mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors disentangle the effect of space charge layer width and built-in electric field on charge dynamics using in-situ time-resolved techniques.
item.dc:title: Disentangling the effect of space and electric field on photoelectrochemical water splitting

item.title: CG14075/Mmt promotes amino acid catabolism and cooperates with AKH during starvation in Drosophila
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77687-7

How animals survive without food depends on more than stored fat and sugar. This study shows that the fruit fly hormone CG14075/Marmite helps redirect amino acid use during starvation, working with a key hormone, AKH, to sustain energy balance.
item.dc:title: CG14075/Mmt promotes amino acid catabolism and cooperates with AKH during starvation in Drosophila

item.title: Loss of oxytocin receptor function disrupts neural signatures of pair bonding and fidelity in the nucleus accumbens
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76876-8

Oxytocin receptor signaling in the nucleus accumbens supports pair bonding, but its role in attachment-related neural activity is unclear. Here, the authors show that Oxtr loss sex-specifically alters pair bonding and nucleus accumbens activity in prairie voles; in males, early activity predicts partner preference.
item.dc:title: Loss of oxytocin receptor function disrupts neural signatures of pair bonding and fidelity in the nucleus accumbens

item.title: Widespread declines of formerly common species reshape local assemblages over time
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77501-4

Human-driven environmental change is reshaping ecological communities worldwide. Analysing 4,748 sites across 129 studies, we show that formerly common species decline disproportionately compared to rare species in marine and terrestrial assemblages.
item.dc:title: Widespread declines of formerly common species reshape local assemblages over time

item.title: Reprogramming the Rossmann fold signature motif creates orthogonal redox biocatalysts
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77633-7

Developing NMN⁺ as an orthogonal redox cofactor could help biomanufacturing approach theoretical maximum yields. Here, the authors show that engineering the Rossmann fold can convert NAD(P)-dependent enzymes to selectively use the noncanonical cofactor NMN(H).
item.dc:title: Reprogramming the Rossmann fold signature motif creates orthogonal redox biocatalysts

item.title: A single-nucleus atlas of ligular region uncovers brassinosteroid-driven cell fate transitions controlling leaf angle in maize
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77393-4

Here the authors integrate single-nucleus transcriptomic and cellular analyse to reveal that brassinosteroid drives cell division, elongation, and subsequent lignification in the ligular region, thereby controlling leaf angle diversity in maize.
item.dc:title: A single-nucleus atlas of ligular region uncovers brassinosteroid-driven cell fate transitions controlling leaf angle in maize

item.title: Two-dimensional metal oxide polaritonics
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77629-3

Metal oxides support a broad range of polaritons. In this review, the authors extend this to the emerging family of two-dimensional metal oxides and cover the impact of crystal structure and extrinsic manipulation on the polaritons along with synthesis approaches and future photonics applications.
item.dc:title: Two-dimensional metal oxide polaritonics

item.title: Leveraging high-throughput proteomics and AI-based protein folding to accelerate VAV1 molecular glue discovery
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77657-z

VAV1 is a blood-cell signaling protein linked to leukemia and autoimmune disease. Here, the authors discover CRBN molecular glues that degrade VAV1 via a non-canonical degron, using proteomics and AI-based structural modeling to guide the design of more potent degraders.
item.dc:title: Leveraging high-throughput proteomics and AI-based protein folding to accelerate VAV1 molecular glue discovery
